newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
White sugar futures in London ended lower in featureless trade. December lost $2.40 to close at $304.5 per tonne while March gave up $1.20 to close at $304.0.
In New York raw sugar futures ended higher across the board with front month March adding 7 points to close at 10.40 cents/lb. May closed 4 points higher to end at 10.48 cents/lb.

Hopes that Russia will appear as a major buyer on the world market during the last quarter of this year have to be buried as the domestic market is awash with Ukrainian and domestically produced white sugar. There were rumours that Russia might have bought up to seven cargos of sugar recently, but that seems to be unlikely, as prices in Russia are around $400 per tonne with Ukrainian sugar even slightly cheaper even with the 10 per cent VAT while imported sugar of European origin costs between $500 to $650 per tonne.

Trade sources said that Russia has 600,000 to 700,000 tonnes of refined sugar, much of it from the Ukraine, in warehouses. Lower production prospects both in Russia and the Ukraine had raised hopes that Russia would import significant quantities, but the country cannot be expected to begin buying in earnest before the second quarter of 1997.

SWITZERLAND - Sugar imports in 1995/96 (October/September) hit record highs. Sugar imports in September 1996 amounted to 15,932 tonnes raw value, up from last year's 10,846 tonnes. This brought total imports in 1995/96 (October/September) up to 169,873 tonnes, up on last year's 155,620 tonnes and 151,377 tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of origin in 1995/96 were Germany with 90,521 tonnes whites against 97,535 tonnes and France with 60,850 tonnes up from 39,414 tonnes. Sugar exports in 1995/96 amounted to 633 tonnes down from 769 tonnes in 1994/95 and 615 tonnes in 1993/94.

SINGAPORE - Sugar imports in July 1996 amounted to 31,829 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 25,614 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1996 (January/July) up to 168,296 tonnes against 149,441 tonnes in January/July 1995. Total import in calendar year 1995 amounted to 271,334 tonnes against 285,420 tonnes in 1994.

Major countries of origin in January/July 1996 were Thailand with 80,000 tonnes raws against 8,000 and Fiji with 20,000 tonnes compared to nil. The major supplier of white sugar in the same period was Malaysia with 40,825 tonnes against 27,774 tonnes.

Sugar exports in January/July 1996 reached 6,892 tonnes, down from 12,021 tonnes exported in the corresponding period the previous year. Total export in 1995 reached 22,136 tonnes against 23,391 tonnes in 1994. The major country of destination in January/July 1996 was Myanmar with 1,187 tonnes whites against 1,026 tonnes.

The European Union awarded 104,350 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 46.721 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on Wednesday. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to November 6 reached 915,950 tonnes, which compares to 1,144,525 tonnes last year.
Tunisia bought a cargo of 14,000 tonnes 45 ICUMSA white sugar for shipment in August 1997. The price was not disclosed.
